title.narrative: Design support gender institutions with JäMy

description.narrative: Insatsen är ett designstöd, dvs ett mindre stöd till svenska Jämställdhetsmyndigheten för att de tillsammans med sin systermyndighet i Bosnien och Hercegovina ska designa ett nytt program. Målet med designstödet är att etablera och hitta former för fördjupat samarbete mellan svenska Jämställdhetsmyndigheten och dess motsvarigheter i Bosnien och Hercegovina, samt att utveckla och lämna in en ny programansökan till ambassaden i Sarajevo.

The contribution is a design support, i.e. a small support to the Swedish Gender Equality Agency for them to design a new program together with their sister agency in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The goal of the design support is to establish and find forms for in-depth cooperation between the Swedish Gender Equality Agency and its counterparts in Bosnia and Herzegovina, as well as to develop and submit a new program application to the embassy in Sarajevo.

To explore a partnership with the Agency for Gender Equality in Bosnia and Herzegovina (BiH) for mututal learning, institutional strengthening and capacity development, as well as enhancing gender equality and women's rights in BiH through comprehensive gender mainstreaming and technical assistance.
Expected results: - A joint, comprehensive programme proposal and its submission to Sida. - Established modalities and scope of agency-to-agency collaboration.

sector.narrative: Women’s rights organisations and movements, and government institutions

description.narrative: The funding for a design phase project was granted for the period 15th of May 2023 to 31st of December 2023. A programme proposal (Sweden Bosnia and Herzegovina Partnership Programme on Gender Equality 20242029 GEAR UP for Results!) was jointly developed by the two Agencies and in close cooperation with the Gender Centres in the Federation of BiH and Republika Sprska entities and successfully submitted on the 31st of January 2024. After a first review of the proposal, the Embassy requested further details on key activities and elaboration on the capacity mapping, along with a risk analysis exercise. Hence, an amendment to the agreement was signed to extend the design phase to 31st May 2024. This was later further extended until 21st of June 2024 during a meeting with the Embassy in Sarajevo in May. And again, later due to key staff being on leave, extended until 30th of June 2024. A final updated programme proposal was submitted 30th of June 2024. The design phase project application outlined various stages of programme formulation, e.g. initial contacts and mapping, including factfinding missions and capacity mapping and needs assessments stakeholder workshops and dialogues agency high level exchange/meetings analysis, consolidation and drafting, and submission of a full programme proposal including budget. The analysis and consequently the development of the programme proposal took into account the findings of the evaluation of the Sidafunded FIGAP project implemented during December 2009 until December 2024. As part of the programme planning a risk analysis exercise was carried out. It will be included in a risk management/mitigation plan which will be further developed during an inception period of the programme. To assess the identified risks a template was used to categorise the risks (low, medium, high and very high) and the identified risks were clustered into five main categories: political, operational, management, financial and unforeseen risks (force majeure). Among the political risks are political changes, economic crisis and a deteriorating security situation. Lack of willingness from relevant institutions and key stakeholders to integrate gender equality is one example of an operational risk potentially affecting implementation. As for the financial and management risks the necessary human and financial resources along with proper management and reporting on funds, is a perquisite for programme implementation, together with the need for external donor engagement and funding. A risk matrix is included in the programme proposal. Risk management will also form part of the programme cycle and is closely interlinked with management of results. It forms part of an adaptive and learning approach to programme implementation. Key to risk management is an integrated approach and risk evaluation will be conducted regularly, at minimum on an annual basis when plans for the upcoming year are made, to capture critical risks and to ensure that proper mitigation efforts are in place. The evaluation of risks will be reported to the Joint Steering Committee each year. A detailed timeline for planned activities 2024 2029 will be developed during the inception period specific to each component of the programme and will form a part of the overall results matrix.
